name: The dot over the i is called a tittle

hook_variants.template: That dot over the i has a name. Nobody knows it.
What is the dot above the letter i actually called?
The dot over 'i' and 'j' is a tittle. It has its own tiny name.

sections.text: The superscript dot on the lowercase i and j is called a 'tittle'.
It started as a scribe's mark to tell adjacent i's apart before typewriters and printers standardized it.
sections.title: origin

sections.text: Other languages got creative: Turkish has a dotted i AND a dotless ı with different sounds.
sections.title: bonus

sections.text: The word 'tittle' is also in the phrase 'jot and tittle' — meaning very small details.
sections.subtitle: and tittle — the tiniest details

sections.text: Next time you type an i, you're typing a tittle. You're welcome.
Follow for more facts hiding in plain sight.

facts.claim: The tittle is the superscript dot found above the lowercase i and j
The tittle originated as a scribal mark to distinguish adjacent i's in handwriting
'Jot and tittle' is an idiom referring to the smallest details

titles: The dot over the i has a name
The tittle: the smallest named thing in your keyboard
